title: talfahrt – software engineering, web apps and backends
description: talfahrt: software development from the Wuppertal area, Germany. Web apps for the phone, backends in Java and Spring Boot, integrations with ERP and invoicing systems. Projects, services and contact.

hero.claim: Software engineering from the Wuppertal area, Germany
hero.lede: Web apps for the phone, backends in Java and Spring Boot, integrations that just run – software that feels light.

projects.title: Projects
projects.intro: My own web apps, live on talfahrt.dev – from idea to prototype in hours, in production within days.

gruppetto.description: The all-in-one app for Grand Tour fans: stage predictions with bonus rankings and joker limits, a live leaderboard for your own group, results and classifications pulled in automatically after every stage, news, stage pages with elevation profiles, climbs and start lists – and 3D mini games where the group races each other. Mobile first, installable from the home screen.
gruppetto.stack: React, TypeScript, Supabase, WebGL, GitHub Actions

rosenherz.description: Clara and Mia inherit Rosenherz Castle and turn it back into a home, room by room. Every room is a 3D dollhouse, every graphic drawn in code, playable offline.

neontd.description: 8 worlds, 48 hand-built tracks, a weekly arena with a global leaderboard. The game logic is written in Java and runs on iPhone, in the browser and as a desktop app.

services.title: Software solutions
services.intro: Software development for companies and teams: from idea to prototype in hours, to a finished solution in production within days. Remote, per project or ongoing.

items.title: Web apps that feel like apps
items.text: Fast, offline-capable, launched from the home screen – no app store, no bloat. Made for the phone, good on the desktop.

items.title: Backend and interfaces
items.text: Java and Spring Boot, REST with OpenAPI, PostgreSQL or Oracle. Production-critical, documented and tested.

items.title: Cloud and operations
items.text: Kubernetes, Azure or AWS, CI/CD, monitoring with Grafana, Prometheus and Loki. Deployments nobody notices.

items.title: Performance
items.text: Caching, database tuning, load behaviour under real numbers. Response times that are measured rather than guessed.

items.title: Integration
items.text: ERP connections, partner interfaces, event streams with Kafka, e-invoicing and reporting obligations. Imports that run at night and report in the morning.

items.title: Modernisation
items.text: From Java 8 to current releases, from COBOL, Delphi or SVN to Java, .NET and Git, from one cloud to another – step by step, without stopping the business.

profile.title: About talfahrt
profile.intro: talfahrt is a software studio near Wuppertal, Germany: one software developer, everything from one pair of hands. It builds back-office systems in Java and Spring Boot, integrations with ERP and invoicing systems, and its own web apps with React, Supabase and WebGL.

contact.title: Let's talk.
contact.text: For projects, enquiries and everything in between.

notFound.title: Page not found

architectures.title: Architectures
architectures.intro: Patterns that have proven themselves in production – as living sketches, computed live in your browser.

items.title: A cluster that breathes with the load
items.text: When requests rise, new instances spin up. When it calms down, they scale back – carefully, so nothing flaps. Response times stay steady, the bill stays small.
items.stack: Kubernetes, Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, Prometheus, Grafana

items.title: A cache layer between database and frontend
items.text: What is already known, the middleware answers within milliseconds; only the rest goes to the database. When a record changes, exactly that entry is dropped – not the whole cache.
items.stack: Spring Boot, Spring Cache, Redis, Oracle, PostgreSQL

items.title: Deployment without downtime
items.text: The new version starts next to the old one, passes its health checks and only then takes over traffic. Instance by instance, with a way back – users notice nothing.
items.stack: Kubernetes, rolling updates, readiness probes, CI/CD

items.title: Events instead of file exchange
items.text: ERP, shop and partners write events into a stream, every system reads at its own pace. If a consumer drops out, the messages wait for it – and are never lost.
items.stack: Kafka, ERP integration, partner interfaces, e-invoicing

items.title: Monitoring that speaks up first
items.text: Metrics, logs and alerts in one place. When response times creep up, the system speaks up before anyone notices – and also tells you when everything is fine again.
